html:
SMTO-CMP-0029 — The AI's check is out of date, so SMTO needs a fresh look

GUID: 430409ba-14d2-4599-98cd-b9ba23351cd3
Slug: completion-stale-current-evidence
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI checked something to prove the task worked, but later steps changed it or a newer check exists. An old reading can't show what's true now, so SMTO asked the AI to check again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task still shows Running, wait. SMTO has asked the AI to look at the current state again. A new check after the last change is the only way to show what is true now.
  2. If the task stops as Partial · resumable, send a message asking SMTO to check the current state again and report what it finds. This replaces the old reading with a current one without changing anything.
  3. Only ask for a change to be made again if that new check shows it's missing. Earlier steps may already have made the change, and repeating it could cause problems.

What success looks like

  • The AI reports a fresh check taken after its last change, and the task finishes as Completed.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat the change until a fresh check shows it isn't in place.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A completion check marked current was rejected because stale_reason found its receipt no longer represents current external state (superseded, conflicting, a later write to the same resource, a newer fresh observation, or internal/snapshot data).

What this means

  • A check explicitly requires current state and stale_reason finds that its receipt no longer represents current external conditions. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • A check explicitly requires current state and stale_reason finds that its receipt no longer represents current external conditions.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the check's current flag with intervening effects and the receipt's freshness relation.

How to fix it

  • Read the stale reason in completion_feedback.open_requirements (operation_id, pointer, description). Perform a new current-state observation after the last relevant write and cite that receipt in the check; earlier execution receipts stay valid as history but cannot satisfy a current-state check.
  • Read current state and cite fresh evidence for claims that require current observation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported current observation establishes the required present-state value.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
